title: Integration and Area under a Curve
seo_title: Integration – SSS 3 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Integrate polynomials; evaluate definite integrals; find the area under a curve; find a curve from its gradient. (summary of the NERDC SSS 3 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free SSS 3 maths worksheets on integration: indefinite integrals, the constant c, definite integrals, area under a curve and finding a curve from its gradient. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Add 1 to the power and divide by it.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Integration is the reverse of differentiation.
  • For an indefinite integral, add the constant c.
  • For a definite integral, integrate, put in the top limit, then subtract the value at the bottom limit.

Examples

Example

∫₁³ 2x dx

[x²] from 1 to 3

9 − 1

Answer: 8

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Forgetting + cEvery indefinite integral needs + c.
Multiplying by the new powerDivide by it.
Subtracting in the wrong orderTop limit minus bottom limit.

faq.q: What does a definite integral give?
faq.a: The area under the curve (above the x-axis).

faq.q: Why is there a constant c?
faq.a: Many curves have the same gradient; c picks one of them.

items.q: Find the area enclosed by the curve y = −x² + 5x and the x-axis.
items.e: The curve meets the x-axis at x = 0 and x = 5. ∫ (−x² + 5x) dx from 0 to 5 = 5³/6 = 125/6 square units.
